newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian miners go on strike over wage arrears.
newsitem.headline: Russian miners go on strike over wage arrears.

text.p: About 400,000 Russian coal miners launched a nationwide strike on Tuesday, complaining they had not been paid for months, news agencies quoted trade union officials as saying.
The union officials said some workers had called on Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to quit, blaming his government for the wage delays. They said some miners had not been paid since June.

The officials said 154 out of Russia's 189 coal pits had stopped work. Some miners said they were starting an indefinite stoppage, while others were simply halting deliveries to consumers for 24 or 48 hours.
Other miners say they will join the strike on December 5 unless the government starts tackling their problems.

Interfax news agency said wage arrears in the sector totalled 2.6 trillion roubles, while the government also owed miners 1.5 trillion roubles in subsidies. Consumers owe miners about eight trillion roubles.
Itar-Tass news agency said miners in the Kuzbass region in southern Siberia and in the Far East were among the most active strikers, while many pits in the southern Urals continued work.
But coal mines of the Krasnoyarsk region declined to take part in the strike, and only one pit in the Orenburg region stopped work.
